text: We love the convenience of library apps like Libby, but we often forget that "free" for readers doesn't mean free for the institution. Every digital ebook or audiobook we check out carries a significant hidden maintenance cost. Unlike physical books that last for decades, digital licenses often expire after a set number of borrows. This means libraries must pay repeatedly to renew access just to keep their digital shelves stocked, straining budgets that are already stretched thin between physical collections and vital community programs.
